body: Inbound files are saved under <session cwd>/.cctg/inbox/<UTC date>-<clean name> with a .cctg/.gitignore of "*" created only when absent, temp dir as fallback; rejected temp-only (reads outside the working folder ask Claude Code permission for every photo) and editing the user .gitignore (forbidden by the task).

Hub announces file support as an optional field registered{files} and the agent sends file_offer only to such a hub; rejected sending offers blind (an old hub warns per chunk and it breaks the wire.rs rule that new message types go only to a peer that announced them).

Telegram downloads (getFile + file URL) run in one hub task outside the Scheduler; rejected an Op::GetFile in the single-threaded scheduler (a 20 MB download would hold every chat message behind it; getFile is a read like getUpdates, not a chat message).

A kept file blocks the later messages of its slot until all its chunks are in the link queue, like TASK-017 text; rejected letting text overtake a file (the question about a screenshot would reach Claude before the screenshot).

A worker started after a hand-over sends notifications/tools/list_changed and every worker declares tools.listChanged, so send_file appears without a claude restart; rejected requiring a TASK-040 restart (docs say Claude Code refreshes on list_changed). Not verified live: no interactive claude allowed.
Adding the media fields straight into api::Message tripped clippy large_enum_variant on scheduler::Outcome (Message grew to 728 bytes); fixed by a boxed #[serde(flatten)] MessageMedia.

Hub budget for files from sessions is one file of the largest size (MAX_FILE_BYTES = files::MAX_UPLOAD, 50 MiB); alternative kept by the planner: 100 MiB (two largest files, ~150 MiB peak with the multipart clone).

An accepted file_offer whose chunks stop coming is dropped at the next offer after UPLOAD_IDLE (60 s) and its agent gets file_answer failed; alternatives: a timer tick in the actor, or an agent-side retract message (new wire type). Chosen: lazy check, no new message, no timer.
The inbox .gitignore (*) goes into .cctg/inbox itself, not .cctg: the planner placement hid every new file a project keeps in .cctg from git status (probe scratch/reviewer2/gitignore_probe.out.txt).
Downloads from Telegram are tried up to 3 times on 429 (retry_after capped at 30 s), network errors and 5xx; 4xx stays final. Alternative kept by the planner: no retry, the user resends.

Files from sessions stay in the one serial scheduler (hub law: all sends through one outbound queue); a 50 MB upload can hold other sends up to DOCUMENT_TIMEOUT 120 s. Alternative rejected: a separate upload task outside the scheduler (breaks the law and per-topic FIFO).

A send_file answer pending at a TASK-040 worker hand-over stays unhandled (documented limit): the hub sends update only when the session has no running turn. Alternative deferred: track pending call ids and answer them with an error before Ended::Handover.

First mutation run hung on M20 (refusal retried): the retry test shared one unread link queue across cases, so the fourth hand-over waited for room forever under a paused clock. Fixed the test (a link per case) and reran M19-M23; all killed.

Tried to check whether files::read_upload on Windows treats an existing named pipe path as a regular file by probing a local pipe server; the probe was blocked by the permission classifier, so the pipe case of send_file validation stays unverified (device names NUL, CON, CONIN$, COM1 were checked with a rustc probe: metadata errors, so NotFile).

Verdict NEEDS_WORK on the ended-session file hand-over (repro crev_a_file_downloading_when_its_session_ends_stays_in_the_slot fails: the ended agent gets the file, the slot drops it with a receipt). Alternative considered: SHIP with it as a documented limit like the TASK-040 hand-over one; rejected because it breaks the TASK-017 invariant written at registry.rs:1016-1020 and the fix is local to on_fetched.

minor-3: senders cut files into 64 KiB chunks (files::CHUNK) but receivers keep taking pieces up to 256 KiB (files::MAX_CHUNK), and a kept file whose hand-over a closing link cuts 3 times in a row is dropped with LINK_LOST_NOTICE. Alternative rejected: the review's verbatim CHUNK = 64 KiB for both ends, which makes an Assembly refuse the 256 KiB pieces of a peer built from 96f1e4b (agents outlive hub upgrades).

minor-5: the agent saves a complete file in a spawned task and stops reading hub link events until that file's channel message went to Claude; stdin lines, tool answers and update deadlines keep running. Alternative rejected: keep reading hub events and hold only inbound/file ones in a local queue (more state and a second file could complete while the first saves); cost: a verdict can wait behind one save.

major-1: on_fetched counts a Handed file only when the job's conn is still live_agent(slot); otherwise the message stays in the slot like LinkClosed, and both stay cases call flush so a newer agent that registered during the download gets the file at once. Alternative rejected: stopping fetch::hand between chunks by a flag (the bytes already queued in the old link cannot be taken back anyway).

QA verdict PASS with one low defect: files::read_upload blocks forever on an existing Windows named pipe (metadata says is_file, len 0; read_to_end waits), which would pin the one send_file worker of that agent. Alternative considered: NEEDS_FIXES; rejected because the path must come from Claude as an explicit pipe path and the task criteria all hold.
